stem: Separate samples of $0.02\text{ mol}$ of calcium carbonate and $0.02\text{ mol}$ of barium carbonate are heated until completely decomposed to the metal oxide and carbon dioxide.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State which of these two Group 2 carbonates requires the higher temperature before it begins to decompose. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
After decomposition is complete, the $0.02\text{ mol}$ sample of calcium oxide is taken and added to $2.00\text{ dm}^3$ of water. A solution is formed with no solid present. Dilute sulfuric acid is then added dropwise until a precipitate is seen.

The same procedure is repeated with the $0.02\text{ mol}$ sample of barium oxide, using the same concentration solution of dilute sulfuric acid.

Identify the sample to which most sulfuric acid must be added to cause a precipitate to appear.

Explain your answer. You should refer to the solubilities of the precipitates and relevant energy terms in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the mass, in g, of $\text{CO}_2$ produced by the decomposition of $0.020$ moles of calcium carbonate.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the minimum mass, in g, of propane that would, on complete combustion, produce the same mass of $\text{CO}_2$ calculated in (c)(i). Give your answer to three significant figures.
